'''William H. Parker''' (born 1941) is an American professor of physics and academic administrator at the [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI). Parker's earliest laboratory research involved seminal experiments that refined the precision of the measurements of [[fundamental constants]].<ref name="Landmark Experiments in Twentieth Century Physics">{{cite book | title = Landmark Experiments in Twentieth Century Physics | isbn = 978-0486285269 | author = George L. Trigg| publisher = Dover Publications | year = 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | date = August 1969 | page = 66 | title = Josephson Effect Permits New Look at Fundamental Constants | journal = Physics Today | volume = 22 | issue = 8 | doi = 10.1063/1.3035742 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | volume = 2 | date = 1973 | pages = 215–291 | title = Quantum theory of Josephson radiation | author = D. Rogovin, Marlan O.Scully, P. Lee | doi = 10.1016/0079-6727(73)90006-2 | journal = Progress in Quantum Electronics | bibcode = 1973PQE.....2..215R }}</ref> His later research focused on [[superconductors]] and other aspects of [[solid-state physics]]. In an administrative capacity at UCI, Parker has served in a variety of roles including as Dean, Department Chair, and Vice Chancellor.

== Education and research ==
Parker earned a bachelor's degree from [[Allegheny College]] in 1963.<ref name=ucistories>{{cite web | url = https://ucistories.lib.uci.edu/people/william-parker | title = UCI Stories: William Parker | publisher = UCI Libraries }}</ref> He obtained MS and PhD degrees from the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. He then joined the faculty of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at UCI in 1967 and he has remained there for his entire career. He was a [[Sloan Research Fellow]] from 1968 to 1970.  In collaboration with [[Donald N. Langenberg]] and [[Barry N. Taylor]], Parker used the alternating current [[Josephson effect]] to precisely measure ''e''/''h'', the ratio of the [[elementary charge]] (''e'') to the [[Planck constant]] (''h'').<ref>{{cite journal | title = Determination of ''e''/''h'' using the AC Josephson effect | author = Langenberg, Donald N.; Parker, William Henry; Taylor, Barry N. | journal = Proc. Int. Conf. At. Masses | date = 1967 | pages = 439–460}}</ref><ref name="Physical Review Letters">{{cite journal | title = Measurement of 2''e''/''h'' using the ac Josephson effect and its implications for quantum electrodynamics | author = Parker, William Henry; Taylor, Barry Norman; Langenberg, Donald N. | journal = Physical Review Letters | date = 1967 | volume =18 | issue = 8 | pages = 287–291 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.18.287 | bibcode = 1967PhRvL..18..287P }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Determination of ''e''/''h'', Using Macroscopic Quantum Phase Coherence in Superconductors: Implications for Quantum Electrodynamics and the Fundamental Physical Constants | author = B. N. Taylor, W. H. Parker, and D. N. Langenberg | journal = Rev. Mod. Phys. | volume = 41 | pages = 375–496 | date = 1969 | issue = 3 | doi = 10.1103/RevModPhys.41.375 | bibcode = 1969RvMP...41..375T }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Reassessment of a determination of ''e''/''h'', using macroscopic quantum phase coherence in superconductors | author = Denenstein, Arnold; Finnegan, T. F.; Langenberg, Donald N.; Parker, William Henry; Taylor, Barry Norman | journal = Physical Review B | date = 1970 | volume = 1 | issue = 11 | pages = 4500–4503 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevB.1.4500 | bibcode = 1970PhRvB...1.4500D }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title =Fundamental physical constants | author = Taylor, Barry Norman; Langenberg, Donald N.; Parker, William Henry | journal = Scientific American | date = 1970 | volume = 223 | issue = 4 | pages = 62–78 | doi = 10.1038/scientificamerican1070-62 | bibcode = 1970SciAm.223d..62T | url = http://eprints.uanl.mx/16658/1/26_the_fundamental%20%281%29.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Measurement of ''h''/''m<sub>e</sub>'' using rotating superconductors | author = Parker, W. H.; Simmonds, M. B. | date = 1971 | issue = 343 | pages = 243–348 | journal = Precision Measurement and Fundamental Constants | bibcode = 1971pmfc.conf..243P }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Large-diameter superconducting quantum interference devices for a measurement of ''h''/''m'' | author = Falco, C. M.; Parker, W. H. | journal = Proc. Int. Conf. Low Temp. Phys. | date = 1974 | issue = 4 | pages = 563–567 }}</ref> This ratio could then also be used to refine the value of other fundamental constants such as the [[fine-structure constant]] (''α'').  The new measurement of ''α'' removed a discrepancy between the theoretical and experimental values of the [[hyperfine splitting]] in the ground state of atomic hydrogen, one of the major unsolved problems of [[quantum electrodynamics]] at time.<ref name="Landmark Experiments in Twentieth Century Physics"/><ref name="Physical Review Letters"/>  For this research, Parker received the [[John Price Wetherill Medal]] from the [[Franklin Institute]] in 1975.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.fi.edu/laureates/william-henry-parker | title = The Franklin Institute Awards: William Henry Parker | date = 11 January 2014 | publisher = [[Franklin Institute]] }}</ref>  Parker's other research examined [[Josephson junctions]]<ref>{{cite journal | title = Linewidth of the radiation emitted by a Josephson junction | author = Dahm, Arnold J.; Denenstein, Arnold; Langenberg, Donald N.; Parker, William Henry; Rogovin, D.; Scalapino, Douglas J. | journal = Physical Review Letters | date = 1969 | volume = 22 | issue = 26 | pages = 1416–1420 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.22.1416 | bibcode = 1969PhRvL..22.1416D }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Effect of thermal noise on current-voltage characteristics of Josephson junctions | author = Falco, C. M.; Parker, W. H.; Trullinger, S. E.; Hansma, Paul K. | journal = Physical Review B | date = 1974 | volume = 10 | issue = 5 | pages = 1865–1873 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevB.10.1865 | bibcode = 1974PhRvB..10.1865F }}</ref> and other aspects of low temperature physics including [[quasiparticle]] and [[phonon]] lifetimes,<ref>{{cite journal | title = Effective quasiparticle lifetime in superconducting tin | author = Parker, W. H. | journal = Solid State Communications | date = 1974 | volume = 15 | issue = 6 | pages = 1003–1005 | doi = 10.1016/0038-1098(74)90518-3 | bibcode = 1974SSCom..15.1003P }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Quasiparticle and phonon lifetimes in superconducting lead films | author = Jaworski, F.; Parker, W. H.; Kaplan, S. B. | journal = Physical Review B | date = 1976 | volume = 14 | issue = 9 | pages = 4209–4212 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevB.14.4209 }}</ref> quasiparticle energy distribution in superconducting films,<ref>{{cite journal | title = Experimental determination of the quasiparticle energy distribution function in optically perturbed superconducting films | author = Jaworski, F.; Parker, W. H. | journal = Physical Review B | date = 1979 | volume = 20 | issue = 3 | pages = 945–951 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevB.20.945 | bibcode = 1979PhRvB..20..945J }}</ref> surface [[Electrical impedance|impedance]],<ref>{{cite journal | title = Study of the temperature dependent anomalous surface impedance of copper | author = Love, David P.; Van Degrift, Craig T.; Parker, W. H. | journal = Proc. Int. Conf. Low Temp. Phys., 14th  | date = 1975 | volume = 3 | pages = 106–109 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Electronic relaxation rates of copper, aluminum, and potassium determined from the temperature dependence of the anomalous surface impedance | author = Love, David P.; Van Degrift, Craig T.; Parker, W. H. | journal = Physical Review B | date = 1982 | volume = 26 | issue = 10 | pages = 5577–5589 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevB.26.5577 | bibcode = 1982PhRvB..26.5577L }}</ref> and [[thermal fluctuations]] in superconducting materials.<ref>{{cite journal | title = Thermal Fluctuations in Superconducting Weak Links | author = M. Simmonds and W. H. Parker | journal = Phys. Rev. Lett. | year = 1970 | volume = 24 | issue = 16 | pages = 876–879 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.24.876 | bibcode = 1970PhRvL..24..876S }}</ref>

== Administration and teaching ==
At UCI, Parker has been Associate Vice Chancellor (1984 to 2000), Vice Chancellor for Research (2000–2006), Dean of Graduate Studies (2000 to 2006), Chair of the Department of Physics and Astronomy (2007 to 2012), and president of the university's Irvine Campus Housing Authority (1983–1990).<ref name=ucistories/> He has won the Daniel G. Aldrich Jr. Distinguished University Service Award (1980 and 2008) and the UCI Medal (2009),<ref>{{cite web | url = http://advancement.uci.edu/medal/index.php | title = UCI Medal Awards | quote = 2009: William Parker, Ph.D.  Professor who transformed fundamental physics and campus housing models through five decades of service to UC Irvine }}</ref> UCI's highest award.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.physics.uci.edu/awards | title = Faculty Honors & Awards | publisher = UCI Department of Physics and Astronomy | quote = UCI Medal (the highest honor awarded by UCI) ... William Parker, 2009}}</ref> Parker has twice won the School of Physical Sciences Outstanding Teacher Award.<ref name=ucistories/>

Parker is coauthor of the book ''The Fundamental Constants and Quantum Electrodynamics''.<ref>{{cite book | title = The Fundamental Constants and Quantum Electrodynamics | author = B. N. Taylor, William H. Parker, D. N. Langenberg | publisher = Academic Press | date = 1969}}</ref>
